title: Release Signal: Ops Digest and Tempo Notes
content:
Release Signal — Ops Digest (weekly)

Meeting date: 2025-11-12
Scribe: Aisha Raman
Attendees: Marco Lin (Release Eng), Priya Singh (SRE), Evan Carter (Serving Runtime), Diego Morales (Platform Eng), Lila Park (Product)
Duration: 45m

Purpose
Short catch-up to align on the release train tempo, hotfix triage status, changelog hygiene, and near-term rollout readiness for the model-v2.1 experiment window.

Agenda
1) Pulse: hotfix queue and lead indicators
2) Canary schedule for model-v2.1 (blue/green and progressive percent rollout)
3) Changelog consolidation and user-facing notes
4) Capacity/slot forecasting for Dedicated pools during surge window
5) Any-blockers, decisions, and action items

1) Hotfix queue and triage
- Current queue size: 7 tickets (priority breakdown: 2 P0, 3 P1, 2 P2). P0s: RINF-2147 (KV cache eviction causing token stutters), RINF-2199 (TLS cert rotation edge-case for private deploy).
- Aging: two tickets >72h (RINF-2115, RINF-2123) — flagged for acceleration.
- Triage notes: we confirmed RINF-2147 reproducer from a steady-state trace; Evan to push detailed reproducer and perf flame graph to the ticket by 2025-11-13.
- Temporary mitigation: turned on conservative KV-eviction policy for affected Dedicated pools (note: increases tail latency slightly; communicated via #dedicated-ops). Rollback plan pinned in RINF-2147.

2) Canary schedule for model-v2.1
- Canary window: start 2025-11-19 09:00 PST, initial 0.5% traffic, evaluate 4h metrics (latency P95, error rate, token cost delta), then 5% after green signal for 24h.
- Canary owners: Marco (canary orchestration), Priya (observability & alerts), Lila (product-level quality signoff).
- Canary thresholds defined:
  - P95 latency increase <= 12% vs baseline
  - Error rate not exceeding baseline + 0.1%
  - Mean tokens/call delta within +/- 2% of baseline
- Fallback policy: automated rollback at threshold breach, manual rollback if degradation persists >30m despite mitigations.
- Feature flags: model routing will be scoped by route-tag to avoid affecting reserved Dedicated workloads.

3) Changelog consolidation
- Problem: recent releases had divergent changelog styles; customers saw ambiguous impact notes for Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Decision: adopt a two-part changelog template for release notes going forward: (a) Customer-impact summary (plain language), (b) Technical details & rollout timeline (for platform teams). Template posted to Confluence (linked_artifacts: confluence:RINF-RELEASE-TEMPLATE).
- Action: Diego to reformat Draft Release Notes for v2.1 and circulate by 2025-11-15. Lila to approve customer-facing copy by 2025-11-17.

4) Capacity/slot forecasting
- Forecast window: 2025-11-19 to 2025-11-26 (canary + initial ramp). Expected 20% burst in dedicated reservations due to internal load tests.
- Current Dedicated spare capacity: 18% across regions; targeted buffer: 10% after canary. Risk if internal load tests hit earlier than scheduled.
- Action: Priya to coordinate with Platform Eng to reserve additional burst capacity (approx 40 GPU-hours across us-west1 and europe-west3) by 2025-11-18. Diego to confirm procurement or reallocation.

5) Any blockers and cross-team dependencies
- Network egress rule tweak in eu-west3 needed before canary traffic will hit that region (ticket: RINF-2205). Blocker owner: Diego. ETA 2025-11-16.
- Observability tweak: event tagging for model-version in tracing needed to correlate token cost regressions. Priya to ship lightweight trace attribute by 2025-11-14.
- Legal/compliance: for private deployments with KMS, we must include rotation notes for the change log. Lila to sync with Security on wording by 2025-11-15.

Decisions made
- Use progressive canary thresholds as listed; automated rollback enabled for metric breaches.
- Consolidated changelog template adopted, must be used for all release trains starting v2.1.
- Hotfix mitigation preference: short conservative config toggles in prod while reproducer is being developed (avoids emergency code pushes when possible).

Action items (owner — due)
- Evan Carter — attach KV cache reproducer, perf flame graphs to RINF-2147 (2025-11-13)
- Priya Singh — reserve burst GPU-hours and implement trace-model-version tag (2025-11-14 / 2025-11-18 respectively)
- Diego Morales — produce reformatted release notes draft and confirm region egress change (2025-11-15 / 2025-11-16)
- Marco Lin — finalize canary orchestration runbook and alert pages; dry-run on staging (2025-11-17)
- Lila Park — approve customer-facing changelog language (2025-11-17)
- Aisha Raman — coordinate post-canary retrospective slot and capture preliminary metrics (2025-11-25)

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: KV cache mitigation increases tail latency and may impact SLOs for interactive customers. Mitigation: limit conservative eviction to affected clusters and monitor SLO delta; escalate if >5% breach.
- Risk: Unexpected Dedicated capacity consumption from internal tests. Mitigation: gate internal heavy tests with capacity tags and schedule outside canary ramp windows.
- Risk: Changelog confusion across customers. Mitigation: single template + targeted customer comms for Dedicated customers with explicit timeline.

Follow-ups for next meeting (2025-11-18 weekly slot)
- Canary dry-run summary and any adjustments to thresholds
- Hotfix queue status and closure of RINF-2115 / RINF-2123
- Capacity confirmation and final release notes

Notes to self / freeform
- Consider adding a lightweight scoreboard for release owners (green/yellow/red) to the weekly email so product and sales can quickly scan.
- Recording location: drive/meeting-recordings/release-ops/2025-11-12.mp4
